quickAnswer.question: How much does a Dubai package cost from Trivandrum?
quickAnswer.answer: iWay Tourism's Dubai packages from Trivandrum start at ₹40,000 per person for a budget 4N/5D trip covering city highlights. The standard 5N/6D package with desert safari, Marina cruise, and premium hotel ranges from ₹50,000–₹60,000. All packages include return flights from TRV, UAE visa processing, hotel accommodation, airport transfers, sightseeing, and a dedicated coordinator.

overview: Dubai is the closest luxury international destination for South Indians — a 4-hour direct flight from Trivandrum that deposits you into a city engineered for spectacle. The world's tallest building, the world's largest shopping mall, man-made islands visible from space, and a desert that transforms into an adventure playground at sunset. For high-net-worth travellers from the Kanyakumari and Trivandrum corridor, Dubai offers accessible opulence without the 12-hour flights that European luxury demands.

iWay Tourism's Dubai packages are built to maximise the experience within 5–6 days. We avoid the trap of cramming everything into a schedule that leaves you exhausted. Instead, the itinerary alternates high-energy experiences (desert safari, theme parks, shopping marathons at Dubai Mall) with deliberate downtime (pool mornings at the hotel, leisurely Marina walks, an unhurried dinner cruise). The result is a trip that feels luxurious in pace, not just in setting.

visaInfo.heading: Dubai (UAE) Visa for Indian Passport Holders

quickAnswer.question: Do Indians need a visa for Dubai?
quickAnswer.answer: Yes. Indian passport holders require a tourist visa for the UAE. The visa is processed electronically — no embassy visit or passport submission required. Processing takes 3–5 working days. iWay Tourism handles the complete visa application as part of the package, including form preparation, document upload, and status tracking.

body: The UAE tourist visa for Indian nationals requires: valid passport (minimum 6 months validity), passport-size photograph against white background, confirmed return flight booking, hotel reservation, and proof of financial means (bank statement or salary certificate).
Visa types: 30-day single entry (standard for tourism), 60-day multiple entry (for extended visits). The 30-day visa is included in iWay's standard packages.
Processing: 3–5 working days. Express processing (24–48 hours) is available at additional cost. iWay Tourism submits the application and tracks approval.

bestTimeToVisit.heading: Best Time to Visit Dubai

quickAnswer.question: When is the best time to visit Dubai from India?
quickAnswer.answer: November to March is the ideal period — temperatures range from 20–28°C, outdoor activities like desert safaris and Marina walks are comfortable, and the Dubai Shopping Festival (January–February) offers significant retail discounts. Avoid June–August when temperatures exceed 45°C and outdoor activity is severely limited.

bestTimeToVisit.body: Dubai's climate is desert — hot summers and mild winters. November to March is peak tourist season for good reason: the weather is perfect for outdoor attractions, hotel pools, and desert excursions. The Dubai Shopping Festival in January–February adds retail appeal. April and October are shoulder months with slightly warmer weather but lower hotel prices. From June to August, temperatures exceed 45°C and outdoor activity is confined to early mornings and late evenings — but indoor attractions (malls, aquariums, theme parks) are fully air-conditioned and tourist crowds are minimal.

faqs.question: Is Dubai expensive for Indian travellers?
faqs.answer: Dubai is mid-range to premium depending on your choices. Accommodation is the largest cost — 4-star hotels in Marina/Downtown run ₹6,000–₹12,000 per night (covered in iWay packages). Food ranges from ₹400–₹600 at food courts and casual restaurants to ₹2,000+ at fine dining. The metro is affordable (₹25–₹80 per ride). Shopping varies enormously — the Gold Souk offers competitive gold prices by weight. Overall, a Dubai trip is more expensive than Vietnam or Sri Lanka but offers a distinctly premium experience.

faqs.question: What dress code applies in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Dubai is cosmopolitan and relaxed in tourist areas — Western clothing is normal at hotels, malls, and beaches. At the Sheikh Zayed Mosque (Abu Dhabi), women must cover their hair, arms, and legs; men must wear long trousers. Free abayas and sheila are provided at the mosque entrance. At beach clubs and pools, standard swimwear is acceptable. In Old Dubai and local markets, modest clothing (shoulders and knees covered) is respectful.

faqs.question: Can I combine Dubai with another destination?
faqs.answer: Yes. The most popular combination is Dubai + Abu Dhabi (included in our premium package). For longer trips, Dubai + Oman (Muscat is 4 hours by road) or Dubai + Sri Lanka (connecting flights via Colombo) are excellent options. Contact iWay Tourism for custom multi-destination itineraries.
